name: Hugo
description: The Alpine spritz: prosecco, elderflower, soda and lime over ice in a wine glass. Lighter and less bitter than an Aperol Spritz.
history: Roland Gruber created it in 2005 at San Zeno bar in Naturns, South Tyrol, first with lemon-balm syrup. Elderflower took over as it spread through northern Italy, Austria and Germany, and it is now the default summer spritz across the Alps.
whyItWorks: Elderflower gives prosecco a floral, lychee-and-pear sweetness; lime and soda keep it from cloying. Mint is the traditional finish when you have it.
steps: Squeeze two lime wedges into a wine glass and drop them in.
Add St-Germain and fill with ice.
Top with prosecco, then soda, and stir once gently.
Slap a mint sprig and tuck it in, if you have mint.
techniqueNotes: St-Germain is sweeter than the elderflower syrup most Italian bars use, so 0.75 oz is plenty.
creator: Roland Gruber
